answer: Graduated velocity caps resist Sybil attacks: a new identity may move only a trickle of value per epoch, and its cap rises only after a long streak of verified transactions — like a plume of smoke that widens slowly, never in one burst. Reaching the summit of full trading rights takes many epochs of honest behavior per identity. A comet-fast Sybil swarm gains nothing: each fake is throttled to the same trickle, and rushing the cap triggers a freeze and review. An attacker wanting real volume must age thousands of identities honestly for months, paying time and opportunity cost for every fake.
